title: QFactorial Leads Project To Apply Quantum Computing To Supply Chains
excerpt: QFactorial leads a project applying quantum computing to supply chain optimization with a $1 million boost from the Australian Government.
content:
Australian supply chains will be the testing ground for new quantum computing applications, supported by $1.12 million in funding from the Department of Industry, Science and Resources’ Critical Technologies Challenge Program. QFactorial leads the 15-month project, partnering with IBM Quantum, Amazon Web Services and Fujitsu to trial quantum solutions for freight efficiency with industry partners.

Professor Muhammad Usman of Monash University’s Faculty of Information Technology explains, “Australia has considerable strengths in quantum research but translating that expertise into technologies that industry can adopt is an important next step,” as researchers focus on making quantum algorithms more resilient to noise.

QFactorial Project Leverages Quantum Optimization for Freight Logistics

QFactorial’s approach to freight logistics will integrate error correction techniques, aiming to improve the stability of quantum algorithms as they scale for commercial use. The collaboration focuses on mitigating quantum noise, a significant impediment to reliable computation in emerging quantum hardware, and will tailor these corrections to the specific circuits used by QFactorial. Tavis Bennett, QFactorial Chief Scientist and Co-Founder, emphasized the importance of this step for achieving commercially viable scale.

These trials will assess quantum solutions for optimizing delivery routes, managing vehicle loads and improving overall freight efficiency, moving beyond theoretical modelling to real-world implementation. The project has secured $1.12 million, emphasising the Australian government’s commitment to supporting a domestic quantum technology ecosystem and addressing national priorities. “Our research will develop innovative quantum methods enabling larger-scale quantum optimisation for complex logistics problems where finding high-quality classical solutions within operational time constraints remains challenging,” he said.

The team intends to address scenarios where conventional computational methods struggle to find optimal solutions within acceptable timeframes, potentially unlocking significant improvements in efficiency and cost savings for freight operators. The project’s findings are expected to inform the future commercial deployment of quantum-enabled optimisation technologies across Australian industry, building on QFactorial’s existing proprietary quantum optimisation heuristics.
